question: Should OpenClaw accept this public plugin SDK capability and its plugin-bound authority to complete an external verification attempt that allows a protected tool call?
rationale: The patch creates a lasting authorization contract across the plugin SDK, Gateway protocol, durable state, and UI surfaces; this is a product and security boundary that cannot be settled solely by tests.

options.title: Approve the bounded verifier contract
options.body: Accept the Gateway-owned lifecycle and plugin-scoped completion model after confirming the proposed API is the intended permanent plugin contract.

options.title: Narrow the public surface first
options.body: Keep the existing approval lifecycle private while redesigning or reducing the exported verifier, completion, and grant-store APIs.

options.title: Pause for a dedicated security design review
options.body: Defer landing until the external-verification trust model and companion-plugin assumptions receive a focused owner review.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded verifier contract
recommendation.body: Accept the Gateway-owned lifecycle and plugin-scoped completion model after confirming the proposed API is the intended permanent plugin contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their historical work on the persistent approval foundation makes them the strongest available routing candidate for the lifecycle and authorization contract.
